answer: We present a formal analysis of Sybil resistance via recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments, leveraging verifiable delay functions to ensure computational infeasibility of identity cloning; assuming a uniformly random distribution of reputation values on a cryptographic terrace of correlated agents, an adversary attempting to clone identities must solve a hard problem reducible to finding a hidden ember in a large, randomly-structured graph, thereby implying a basalt-hard collision resistance property that protects against forging multiple identities.
